pages.title: About
pages.description: Why The Agency exists: so a small business can get good work done without learning a new tool.
pages.headline: Built for people who run a business, not a computer.
pages.lede: The Agency exists so a small business can get good work done without learning a new tool.
body: Most owners we talk to are busy and practical. They have a problem and want it gone. They do not want a long proposal or a meeting about the meeting.
So we keep it simple. One point of contact. Plain words. A price you can read in ten seconds. You always see the work before it goes anywhere.
Our guide, Scout, helps you through the steps and answers questions at any hour. Scout is an AI guide, and says so if you ask. The people behind The Agency check the work before you see it.

pages.title: Privacy
pages.description: What The Agency does with the message you send from this site.
pages.headline: What happens to your message.
body: When you use the contact form, your email app opens with your message ready to send. Nothing is sent until you press send in your email app.
This site does not use cookies, analytics or advertising trackers. It is hosted on GitHub Pages, which keeps standard server logs of visits.
We use your message only to reply to you. To ask us to delete it, write to hello@moremarginco.com.

posts.title: How to read a quote in five minutes
posts.summary: What to look for before you say yes to any quote.
body: A good quote answers four questions. What exactly will I get? When will I get it? What does it cost? What happens if I want a change?
If any of the four is missing, ask. A person who has done the work before can answer in a sentence.
Look at what is left out. Photos, text, hosting and later changes are the usual surprises. Ask about each one by name.
Last, check that the price is fixed or capped. An hourly rate with no limit is a guess, and you carry the risk.

posts.title: What a small business website actually needs
posts.summary: Five things a customer looks for, in the order they look.
body: Most visitors arrive with one question: can this business help me? The first screen should answer it in a sentence.
Next they look for proof. A few real examples, a name, a face, a place. Without them they leave.
Then they look for the price or at least a range. You do not need exact numbers, but a hint saves both sides time.
Then how to reach you. Put it in the header and the footer. Make it one click.
Last, they check that the site works on a phone. Most of them are holding one.
